title: Best Menu Designers (2026): How to Hire One for Your Restaurant
description: How to hire a menu designer for a restaurant, cafe or bar: what to include, print and digital menus, how to brief it, price factors and red flags.
intro: A menu is a sales tool as well as a list of dishes. A clear, well-organized menu helps guests decide quickly and can guide attention to the dishes you most want to sell. Menus go wrong when prices and dishes are hard to read, the design cannot be updated easily when prices change, or allergy information is missing or wrong. This guide helps you order a menu that looks good and works in service.

faq.q: Should I have printed and digital menus?
faq.a: Many restaurants need both: a printed menu, a version for delivery apps and a web or QR code version. Ask for all formats you use in the same order.

faq.q: How do I keep prices up to date?
faq.a: Ask for an editable template, so you or your team can change prices and dishes without a new design each time.
Include it clearly, following the rules where you operate. The designer places the information you provide; checking accuracy is your responsibility.

faq.q: How many items should a menu have?
faq.a: Fewer items are usually easier to choose from and to run in the kitchen. The designer can help group items clearly.
It depends on your style. A few high-quality photos can help; many small, poor photos can make a menu look cheap.
